findings.element: New evaluation → Filters card → the five scope selects (Transport Association, Transport Company (TU), Cantons, Lines, Stops)
findings.finding: Every one of the five scope filters offers the same two options, "SBB" and "BLS", so Cantons, Lines and Stops are populated with transport-company names instead of cantons, line numbers and stop names.
findings.user_impact: An authority user scoping an evaluation is shown a canton list containing no canton and a stop list containing no stop, so the scope they believe they set is not the scope the evaluation would run on, and the resulting punctuality figures would be attributed to the wrong dimension.
findings.suggested_fix: Populate each scope select from its own dimension — cantons from the Swiss canton list (Bern, Zürich, …), Lines from line numbers/Linienbündel, Stops from stop codes and names — and keep SBB/BLS only under Transport Company (TU).

evidence.source: Domain rule (MISS-2026-09-16): a sample's shape is a factual claim, not decoration. The app's own glossary defines "TU — Transportunternehmen (transport company)" as a distinct entity from Kanton, Linie and Haltestelle; offering a TU as a canton or a stop is a category error, not placeholder text.

findings.element: New evaluation → Filters card → first scope select label (English UI)
findings.finding: The filter the German UI labels "RPV/OV" is labelled "Transport Association" in English, but RPV/OV is Regionaler Personenverkehr / Ortsverkehr — a transport segment of the QMS, not a Verkehrsverbund (transport association).
findings.user_impact: An English-language authority or TU user filters expecting to narrow by transport association and instead narrows by traffic segment, producing an evaluation whose stated scope does not match what was measured — and the two labels disagree across the language switch for the same control.
findings.suggested_fix: Label it "RPV/OV" in English as well, or "Transport segment (RPV/OV)", and reserve "Transport association" for an actual Verkehrsverbund filter if one is ever added.

evidence.source: The prototype's own glossary string: "RPV — Regionaler Personenverkehr (regional passenger transport)" — the English label renames the domain concept the German label and the glossary both define.

findings.element: Filter bar → Status dropdown option, and the matching status badge in the table's Status column
findings.finding: The running-evaluation status is written "In Progress" with both words capitalised.
findings.user_impact: Minor, but it is the one status that deviates from the house casing rule, so it reads as a different class of thing from "Done" and "Failed" beside it in the same dropdown and column.
findings.suggested_fix: Write it "In progress" in the filter option, the status badge and any aria-label; this is a casing change only, so the precise status term is untouched.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md, "## Statuses — Only first word capitalized (e.g. \"Synced with warnings\")"; the canonical status list spells it "In progress".

gaps: New evaluation → scope selects: the state map records that the page opens but never records a select being opened, so the "SBB"/"BLS" option set in DOM-1 is read from the port's rendering code rather than from an exercised interaction — worth confirming on screen before fixing.
Evaluation-type select on the New evaluation page: the state map does not record it being opened, so whether the six type names there match the six list group headers exactly is unverified.

DPM is never expanded anywhere in the port — the acr_dpm/acr_rpv/acr_tu/acr_dqi glossary strings exist in the port's dictionary but no component consumes them — so a reader of the list cannot learn what DPM means; I could not confirm from the state map whether some other surface supplies it.

"Connection Punctuality" is the only one of the six types with no DPM qualifier while the other five carry it. Whether Anschlusspünktlichkeit genuinely sits outside the DPM measurement programme, or the qualifier was simply dropped, cannot be settled from the state map or the prototype.

The expansion the prototype gives for DPM — "Durchschnittliche Pünktlichkeitsmessung" — could not be checked against a QMS RPV CH source: web search was unavailable in this run. It is asserted by the prototype with no source, so treat it as unverified rather than confirmed.
Live page could not be opened this round (browser tool unavailable), so German rendering was verified from the port's DE dictionary rather than from the running page.
